definition: A type of autoencoder trained with a sparsity constraint, used in interpretability research to decompose a model's internal activations into a larger set of more individually interpretable features.
details: Sparse autoencoders have become a key tool in mechanistic interpretability for addressing the superposition problem, aiming to find a set of sparse, more monosemantic features underlying a model's dense internal representations.

explainer.lead: A sparse autoencoder is an autoencoder trained with a sparsity constraint, used in interpretability research to break a model's internal activations into a larger set of more individually interpretable features. It matters as a key tool for tackling superposition—dense representations hiding many features.

tiers.eli5: It is like unpacking a packed suitcase into many small labelled compartments, so you can see what is actually inside without everything being jumbled together.
tiers.practitioner: Interpretability researchers train sparse autoencoders on a model's activations to surface sparse, more monosemantic features. A pitfall is that the recovered features are an approximation, not a guaranteed faithful account of the model.
tiers.paperLevel: An autoencoder with a sparsity constraint that decomposes dense internal activations into a larger set of sparser features, aimed at addressing the superposition problem.

explainer.example: A researcher feeds a layer's activations into a sparse autoencoder and inspects individual units that activate on distinct, single concepts.
